Subject: RE: [Draft] Customer notification - GPU thermal throttle event

Marissa — thanks, reading in. Quick technical summary:
- Root cause (prelim): a vendor driver update (rolled last night to a subset of us-west-1 nodes) exposed a corner case in the thermal-sensor aggregation. Sensors briefly reported spike values while GPU workload continued; our thermal-protection path engaged conservative throttling.
- Autoscaler interaction: the throttling reduced effective QPS per node. Our cost-driven autoscaler used a short moving-average window and interpreted the reduction as low demand; scale-downs started before warmups could recover.
- Impact surface: ~18 of 120 nodes in the Dedicated pool were affected, concentrated on two racks. Affected customer traffic saw 40–70% throughput degradation and 2–6x latency tail increase for long-context generation.

Immediate technical mitigations I recommend and can enact now:
1) Hotfix: pin driver to previous stable release on affected racks (rollback) — estimated 25–40 minutes to complete and validate.
2) Routing: shift Halcyon routes to us-west-2 warm spare pool (instant, <5 min) while we rollback/validate.
3) Autoscaler: bump the autoscaler sensitivity (longer window, disable aggressive scale-down) while we validate to avoid further evictions.

Ill attach the extracted thermal logs (thermal-logs-20260830.txt) and a short timeline. If you want, I can take the rollback and routing now.

—Karthik

I wanted to notify you directly about an issue that affected your Dedicated capacity this morning and tell you what were doing to stabilize things. Short summary:

- Between 08:42–09:05 PT today a subset of Dedicated GPU hosts serving Halcyon experienced thermal-throttle conditions after a vendor driver update. This reduced token throughput on affected nodes by ~55–70% and caused latency spikes for long-context generation.

Impact

- Rolled back the problematic driver on impacted racks and adjusted the autoscaler sensitivity to prevent premature scale-downs.
- Collected thermal telemetry and request traces; attached a short timeline and log excerpt.

Next steps
- Were validating the rollback and running a soak test for 2 hours. If validation passes we will return traffic to your Dedicated pool with a coordinated cutover and no customer-facing disruption expected.
- Were preparing a preliminary post-incident note for you by end of day today and a fuller postmortem by EOD Monday (2026-08-31).

Compensation

If youd like to hop on a quick call to walk through technical details and timeline, Im available at 10:15–10:45 PT. Please let me know what works.

Apologies for the disruption — we recognize how disruptive this is and are prioritizing a thorough root-cause and follow-up.

Subject: Post-incident: preliminary findings & next steps (Halcyon DL-7782)

Priya —

Attached is our preliminary post-incident summary and next steps (short version here). Thank you for taking the call this morning — that helped us validate some of the traces.

Preliminary findings
- Root cause: regression in vendor GPU driver aggregation code that caused brief false-positive thermal excursions on two racks after last-night rollout. The driver caused the node-level thermal-protection path to throttle clock frequency aggressively.
- Amplifier: autoscaler sensitivity used a 30s window which led to scale-down signals during the throttling period; this reduced warm capacity and extended recovery time.

Actions taken
- Rolled back driver on impacted racks (completed 09:20 PT day of incident).
- Adjusted autoscaler windows to 5m for Dedicated pools for the immediate stabilization window.
- Created a new health-check that distinguishes sensor spikes from sustained thermal events; queued the fix for validation and deployment (ETA: 2026-09-02).
- Began continuous soak and perf validation on the recovered racks; 4-hour soak completed successfully.

Customer impact & credit
- Impact window: 2026-08-30 08:42–09:12 PT.
- Estimated affected requests: 24,300 inference calls.
- Estimated affected tokens: ~4.8M tokens (prelim).
- Proposed credit: 12% of host-hours for the affected Dedicated pool during the billing day (we propose this as an initial offer; open to discussion).

Next steps
- Final postmortem with RCA and attachments (driver traces, autoscaler metrics, orchestration timeline) — target: EOD Monday (2026-08-31) with a final credit calculation.
- 1:1 technical review + Q&A: scheduled for 2026-09-01 10:30 PT (calendar invite sent).
- Preventive: vendor coordination to halt the implicated driver rollout across other regions until fix validated.

Please let me know if you need additional numbers or a formal compensation statement for your finance team. We will follow up with the full artifacts and a formal DocuSign credit agreement if you accept the proposed credit.

Apologies again for the disruption — were treating this as high priority and will provide continuous updates.

Thanks,
